result.title: Right Reason, Wrong Advice: Evaluating Recourse in LLM Explanations of Denied Requests
result.summary: Language models increasingly write the explanations people receive when a rule system denies their request. If several rules deny the request independently, an explanation can name a true reason and still leave the person denied after they fix it. We call the missing property recourse validity: changing what the explanation cites, without changing what was asked for, can flip the decision. We compute it exactly, and a hitting-set argument predicts from the policy alone when a correct reason fails. In six of seven rule systems ported from access control and US benefit eligibility, a single correct reason almost never gives recourse when several reasons apply. Across 20 LLMs, checks of whether the cited reasons are correct, computed or asked of an LLM judge, are close to chance at spotting this failure, as the argument predicts. A strong judge asked whether acting on the explanation would work does spot it. Stronger and reasoning models do better but still fail on many denials with four or more independent reasons. Asking for every rule helps every open model with room to improve. Explanations of eligibility decisions should be built from the decision function and judged by whether acting on them works.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究规则系统拒绝请求时 LLM 撰写的解释是否具备「recourse validity」，即在不改变请求内容的前提下改变解释所指的原因能否翻转决定；作者精确计算该性质，用 hitting-set 论证从策略本身预测「正确原因仍无济于事」的情形，并在 7 个规则系统与 20 个 LLM 上检验模型与 LLM judge 能否识别这种失效。
AI.relevance_reason: 「改变所引内容是否足以翻转决定」这一反事实充分性判据，可能为判断 latent reasoning 中筛选出的视觉证据是否真正必要、充分而非仅表面正确提供一种评价思路，可供核查；但该文限于文本规则决策，与多模态内部状态无直接关系。
